references.text: Context for the sending: Jesus had just given the disciples instructions to find the colt ([ref:Luk 19:29-31|Luke 19:29-31]). Verse 32 confirms that everything happened exactly as Jesus had said, demonstrating his foreknowledge.
A similar pattern where the disciples are sent out and find everything just as Jesus told them, this time in connection with preparing the Passover meal ([ref:Luk 22:13|Luke 22:13]).
The parallel account in [ref:Mark 11:4|Mark 11:4] also describes how the disciples went and found the colt tied, just as Jesus had told them.
The parallel account in [ref:Matt 21:6-7|Matthew 21:6-7] tells that the disciples went and did as Jesus had instructed them, bringing both the donkey and the colt.
Another example of the disciples doing as Jesus commanded and finding everything just as he said, here in connection with preparing the Passover meal ([ref:Matt 26:19|Matthew 26:19]).

In [ref:Mark 14:16|Mark 14:16], the disciples enter the city and find everything just as Jesus had told them, again in connection with the Passover meal – a repeated pattern that underscores Jesus' prophetic authority.
Mary's words "What he says to you, do it" ([ref:Joh 2:5|John 2:5]) illustrate the same principle of acting in obedience to Jesus' word and experiencing things happening just as he said they would.
In [ref:4 Mos 22:28|Numbers 22:28], the Lord speaks through a donkey. God has full control over animals, which is reflected in the fact that the colt stood exactly where Jesus said it would stand.
